Denver as a tax jurisdiction

Since December 1, 1902 Denver has been both a city and a county. Where other places have a city hall and a separate courthouse, here a single government does both jobs. About 715,522 people lived in its 78 official neighborhoods at the 2020 count, with Adams, Arapahoe and Jefferson counties around the edges.

For a seller that means fewer stops. One city government employs the Assessor who prices your house, the Treasury staff who bill it and the Recorder who files the deed. Hail is the weather problem people bring up, because Denver sits tenth among U.S. cities of 50,000 or more for hailstorm exposure. Expect buyers to ask how old the roof is.

How the Denver tax bill is calculated

Take actual value, subtract a value reduction, multiply by an assessment rate, then multiply by the mill levy. The Assessor's FAQ gives these 2024 inputs:

Property typeValue reduction per parcelAssessment rate
Residential$55,0006.7%
Commercial improved$30,00027.9%
All other$027.9%

Denver's combined general mill levy for 2024 came to 79.202 mills, or 0.079202 as a decimal. Taxing authorities settle on levies every December and neither levies nor rates stay put, so rely on your own bill for current numbers.

Real property gets a fresh appraisal in odd-numbered years only. A house is priced by the market approach, which looks at sales in the two years that ended the previous June 30.

Due dates and the yearly calendar

You have two ways to pay: halves on the last day of February and June 15, or a single payment by April 30. Treasury's calendar covers the rest of the year:

  • January: yearly tax statements go in the mail.
  • April 1: last day to apply for a deferral.
  • April 15: personal property declarations.
  • April 30: full payment, plus the cutoff for the elderly and disabled refund application.
  • May through August: notices go to delinquent accounts.
  • July 1: later delinquencies open up for tax lien buyers to endorse.
  • July 15: senior and disabled veteran exemption applications.
  • September and October: delinquent taxes appear in a newspaper notice.
  • October: the real estate tax lien auction.

For an exact payoff on a delinquent account, including penalty and interest, call Treasury.

Protesting your Denver valuation

Mark June 8 on the calendar every year. If it falls on a weekend or holiday you get the next business day. Your Notice of Valuation explains how to submit in writing, in person or online.

A good protest names your parcel or schedule number, gives a phone number you will answer in the daytime, and states plainly why the value is off. Back it up with sales of comparable houses or evidence of problems like a bad foundation or failing roof. Lose, and you can still take it to the State Board of Assessment Appeals, to District Court, or to binding arbitration.

Skipped a protest in the past? You may reach back up to two earlier years with a petition to the Board of County Commissioners for abatement or refund of taxes.

Deferral for seniors and active military

Through the county treasurer, Colorado allows certain owners to put off paying. The application window is January 1 to April 1, and eligible groups are owners 65 or older and active-duty military.

A senior applicant must reach 65 by December 31, occupy the house, be current on earlier taxes, owe no more than 75 percent of actual value in liens and mortgages, and carry no reverse mortgage. Active-duty applicants meet another test: liens, mortgages and deferrals combined must stay below 100 percent of actual value with a VA-guaranteed loan, or 90 percent without.

What you defer is really a loan, recorded behind your mortgage as a junior lien and accruing interest from May 1. Sign a sale contract and repayment comes due within 90 days. Request the payoff figure early so your title company can fold it into closing.

Storm drain and sewer liens

Storm drain and sanitary sewer service are billed on their own statements, and an unpaid one can cling to the property alongside regular tax. Storm drain bills arrive in February, April, June and August; sewer bills in March, May, July and September.

Title searchers will spot any unpaid service lien and list it as a payoff. Get the balance from Treasury before you put the house up. For other city questions, dial 3-1-1, or (720) 913-1311 from outside Denver.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The October lien auction

Taxes that stay unpaid through summer are advertised in September and October, and the real estate tax lien auction follows in October. Buyers at the auction are paying your tax in return for a claim, which then has to be cleared before a clean sale. Delinquency notices start in May, so the sooner you deal with a balance, the fewer steps remain.

If a notice arrives for an account you believe is paid, gather your payment dates and the parcel ID and contact Treasury quickly. A wrong notice left alone can still drift toward the sale list.

What to gather before you list

Pull together your latest tax statement, your Notice of Valuation and any deferral paperwork. Note whether you protested this year and whether a protest is still open. If your mortgage includes escrow, ask the lender for its payment history so the title officer can match it against what Treasury shows.

Sellers who inherited a house should also locate any storm drain or sewer statements, since those are separate from the main bill and easy to miss. Ask the title company early which of the three items, tax, service lien or deferral, show a balance, so no payoff surprises you at the closing table. Seniors and disabled owners who claimed an exemption should confirm it is still in place, because the July 15 application date comes around every year and a lapse can raise the next bill.

Selling with taxes owed

A tax balance is not a barrier to selling. Treasury gives the title company a figure, and the money is taken from your sale proceeds, so nothing comes out of pocket beforehand. Typical order of events:

  1. The current balance is pulled, along with any earlier years still open.
  2. The title search surfaces service liens, a deferral lien and anything sold at the October auction.
  3. Each one turns into a payoff line on the settlement statement.
  4. Treasury is paid when the sale closes.

Once a lien has been sold, the buyer's payoff is owed on top of the tax, which is where an experienced Denver title officer earns their fee. If you think a delinquent notice is wrong, write to propertytaxinfo@denvergov.org with your parcel ID, address and payment dates.

Behind on tax, or inherited a Denver house you don't want? We can send a written cash offer for it in its current condition. A cash sale skips the repairs and showings, and the decision stays with you.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When is Denver property tax due?

Either split it between the last day of February and June 15, or pay it all by April 30. A weekend or holiday pushes the date to the next business day.

What is the Denver property tax protest deadline?

June 8, or the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. Your Notice of Valuation explains how to file.

What was Denver's mill levy in 2024?

Denver's combined general levy came to 79.202 mills. Because levies change each December, check your current bill.

How often does Denver reappraise homes?

In odd-numbered years only. Values reflect sales from the two years ending the previous June 30.

Does selling a Denver house trigger the property tax deferral repayment?

Yes. Under the state program, a sale or contract of sale starts a 90 day clock for repayment.

Who bills property tax in Boulder

Boulder lies against the Rocky Mountain foothills roughly 25 miles northwest of Denver and serves as the Boulder County seat. The city runs no property tax office. The Boulder County Treasurer bills and collects, and the Boulder County Assessor sets the value. Homeowners receive a single bill that totals the levies from each taxing body covering the parcel, including the school district and local governments.

The Treasurer's office is at 1325 Pearl St. in Boulder, and the phone is 303-441-3520.

On the housing side, the city had 105,689 residents in a 2025 estimate, down slightly from 108,250 in 2020. Only 47.2% of homes are owner-occupied, the median home value is $1,039,500 and median gross rent is $2,018. With values that high, the tax bill is large in dollars even when the rate is modest, and a missed payment grows quickly because the penalty is a percentage of the bill. Small percentages add up fast on a bill this size, so it pays to know the date before the month turns.

Older homes and as-is sales

Boulder started as a gold camp when prospectors arrived in late 1858, and the town was incorporated in 1871, so plenty of houses are old and some carry deferred repairs. Selling as-is to a cash buyer avoids the repair haggling that so often stalls a financed sale. Water is the other issue buyers raise. The September 2013 floods put 9.08 inches of rain on Boulder in a single day, and Boulder County had 262 homes destroyed and nearly 300 damaged. Ask your title company and insurer about flood history for any parcel near a creek, and keep your repair records.

Due dates and late interest

You can pay in two halves, due about March 2 and June 15, or in one full payment due April 30. Paying early earns no discount. Late interest is a percentage that depends on the month paid.

Month paidFirst halfFull paymentSecond half
March1%Not lateNot late
April2%Not lateNot late
May3%1%Not late
June 1 to 154%2%Not late
June 16 to 304%2%1%
July5%3%2%
August6%4%3%

For September through December, phone the Treasurer for the current amount. Certified funds are required for delinquent payments and for anything paid after September 1. The postmark date is what counts on a mailed check.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How the bill is figured

Each taxing body multiplies its mill levy by your assessed value, which is the actual value of the home times an assessment rate. A mill equals $1 of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value.

  • Residential, school districts: 7.05% in 2025 and 2026.
  • Residential, local government: 6.25% in 2025 and 6.8% in 2026.
  • In 2026, local government math starts by taking 10% off the first $700,000 of actual value.

Your own bill depends on the districts that cover your address, and the Treasurer's lookup shows the real figure. Before listing, pull the latest bill so you can tell buyers what the taxes run.

How to appeal your assessment

File with the Assessor from May 1 to June 8. The county enforces that window strictly. Filing options are email, mail, fax, the online portal, a drop box in Boulder, Lafayette or Longmont, and the counter at 1325 Pearl St.

Back your appeal with comparable sales and any errors on the property record. Sales from July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024 are the comparison window this cycle. A Notice of Determination follows from the Assessor by August 15, and a written appeal to the Board of Equalization is then possible on or before September 15.

The tax itself is outside the Assessor's reach. City councils, school boards and special districts set the levies, so an appeal can only challenge value.

Selling with taxes owed

Boulder County sells liens on unpaid real property tax at an annual auction held in November, and liens sold in 2026 earn 13% a year. A list of advertised properties is posted by the Treasurer and refreshed every Friday. Mobile home taxes are not auctioned and are struck off to the county.

Each year's tax lien attaches January 1, which makes that year's tax a live item at closing. Anything you owe is paid by the title company out of your proceeds. Request a payoff early, so an unexpected figure does not push back the closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a rental

Every Boulder rental needs a city license, and a sale resets the paperwork. A new owner needs a rental inspection and a new license application.

  • The rental license fee is $190, and inspections are done by private inspectors who set their own prices.
  • Long-term rentals must hold SmartRegs energy certification before the license application is submitted.
  • Owners who live outside Boulder County must name a local agent who can reach the property within 60 minutes.
  • Short-term rentals must be the owner's principal residence and last no more than 29 days, and the license is no longer valid if the property is sold.

A buyer who purchases a rental as-is takes on the licensing step, so a cash buyer is a practical fit for landlords who want out. If tenants are in place, gather the leases before you list, and tell the tenants early about showings. Landlords often find the timing the hardest part: a lease end, a failed inspection or a missing energy certificate can each stretch a sale by weeks, whereas an as-is buyer takes those items on after closing.

Preparing a Boulder house for sale

Start with paperwork. Pull your most recent tax bill, your notice of valuation and any appeal records, and gather the repair history for the roof, the heating system and any flood or water work. Because bills here are large, buyers pay attention to what the yearly tax runs, and a clear answer helps you hold your price.

Next, confirm what is owed. A call to the Treasurer gets you the current balance, and the county's property list shows whether the parcel is advertised for the lien sale. If the house is a rental, confirm the license status and the inspection date, since both reset at sale.

Finally, decide how you want to sell. A traditional listing means showings, buyer inspections and a lender's schedule. A cash sale skips the showings and the loan approval, and closes when you pick the date. Either way, the deed is recorded in Boulder County, and the title company settles the tax payoff from your proceeds.

Closing costs on the seller's side

On the seller's side you will see three charges: any unpaid property tax, the county's documentary fee and the recording fee. The state sets the documentary fee at one cent per $100 of consideration above $500 (C.R.S. 39-13-102), and the county clerk and recorder collects it.

Recording a document in Boulder County costs $43 as of July 1, 2025. The clerk's office is at 1750 33rd St., Suite 201. Before signing, have your title company explain each line of the settlement statement. Questions worth asking: what tax figure was used, whether any interest was added, and who will record the deed and on what day. Those three answers cover most of the surprises sellers report.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When is Boulder property tax due?

Two half payments are due around March 2 and June 15, or one full payment is due April 30. Late interest starts the day after each due date and climbs each month.

Does the City of Boulder collect property tax?

No. The Boulder County Treasurer bills and collects it for every taxing body, and the county Assessor sets the value.

Can I sell my Boulder house if I owe property tax?

Yes. Your sale proceeds normally cover the balance at closing. Call the Treasurer, 303-441-3520, for a payoff number before choosing a closing date.

What is the last day to appeal my Boulder valuation?

The Assessor must receive it by 11:59 p.m. on June 8. If you disagree with the determination, a written Board of Equalization appeal is due by September 15.

Do I need a rental license to sell a Boulder rental?

Not to sell. The next owner, though, must pass an inspection and apply for a new license, and a short-term rental license ends at sale.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Colorado Springs property tax?

Colorado Springs and your tax bill

Sitting below Pikes Peak roughly 70 miles south of Denver, Colorado Springs serves as the county seat of El Paso County. At 195.761 square miles it covers more ground than any other Colorado municipality, and that sprawl shows up on tax bills. A house against the western foothills and a new build on the far east side can land in different school, fire and metro districts, so two homes of equal value can owe different amounts. Homes range from historic districts, a legacy of the town's June 19, 1886 incorporation, to brand new subdivisions.

You will never get a bill from City Hall. The county treasurer's office does the billing and collecting for the city and every other taxing body.

Mill levies on a Colorado Springs bill

One mill means $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and your bill adds up every levy on the parcel. Colorado Springs itself levies 3.009 mills for tax year 2025 (billed in 2026), a drop from 3.554. Other entities, with the prior year for comparison:

  • El Paso County: 6.857 mills, against 6.985.
  • Pikes Peak Library District: 2.938, against 3.140.
  • Colorado Springs Downtown Development Authority: 5 in both years.

Schools take the biggest bite on most bills, and each district sets its own rate separately from other local governments. Tax year 2025 levies:

  • Colorado Springs School District 11: 37.695 mills.
  • Harrison School District 2: 39.989.
  • Academy School District 20: 45.459.
  • El Paso County School District 49: 45.649.
  • Widefield School District 3: 57.682.
  • Fountain-Fort Carson School District 8: 29.765.

The 2026 residential assessment rate for schools is 7.05%. Look at the district named on your statement before you compare your house with a neighbor's across a district line.

Fire, metro and other special districts

Some parcels carry extra levies for fire protection, improvements or a metro district. A few examples for tax year 2025:

  • Broadmoor Fire Protection District: 4.5 mills.
  • Black Forest Fire Protection District: 15.65 mills.
  • Old Colorado City Security and Maintenance District: 13.416 mills.
  • Banning Lewis Ranch Metro District No. 2: 46.469 mills, with neighboring districts at other levels.

Metro districts pay for roads, water and parks in newer subdivisions, and their levies run far above what a city or county charges. Owners in one can see its charge as a separate line, and buyers will ask about it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax dates

The county's yearly calendar is below. A due date landing on a weekend or holiday slides to the following business day.

DateWhat happens
January 10Assessor hands the prior year's tax warrant to the Treasurer
January 28Deadline for mailing statements
Last day of FebruaryFirst half comes due
March 31Senior tax deferral applications due to the State Treasurer
April 30Whole-year payment comes due
June 15Second half comes due; anything unpaid turns delinquent
JulyDelinquency notices go out and interest begins
SeptemberOverdue real estate taxes are advertised ahead of the auction
After September 30Only cash or certified funds accepted
OctoberLiens on overdue real estate taxes are auctioned

Interest on a late bill runs 1% a month. There's no grace period, and the county won't take partial payments. The auction happens online through RealAuction, and bidders register at the end of September.

Ways to pay

How you pay affects whether you are on time, so choose early.

  • Online: current-year taxes through the Property Tax Search and Payment Portal, by credit, debit or ACH.
  • In person: credit or debit card at the office, with card processing fees passed to the cardholder.
  • Mail: current-year payments count as timely with a USPS postmark dated by the due date. A postage meter stamp from your own office won't do.
  • Fixed income: owners can enroll in monthly payments through EscrowTaxes.
  • Tax liens and redemptions: pay with cash, a cashier's check or a money order. A postmark won't save a late one.

Cards stop being accepted for current-year taxes after September 30. The statement is mailed to the owner of record rather than the lender, so if you have a mortgage, ask whether the lender holds your taxes in escrow.

How to challenge your assessment

Call first. The County Assessor (1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300) wants an informal talk before any formal appeal, and the number is (719) 520-6600.

When a call doesn't settle it, the Board of Equalization is next, reached through the Clerk to the Board in Suite 2201 down the hall, (719) 520-6430. Protests on real property must reach the Board by July 15. Teams hearings fill July 6 through August 5. You and the county each present for 10 minutes, the burden of proving value sits with you, and the written ruling follows within five business days.

  • Your evidence must be market data dated January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, the window behind the 2025 and 2026 values.
  • Beyond the Board you can choose the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court or arbitration, filed inside 30 days of the ruling.
  • Court filings go to the Fourth Judicial District Court, 270 S. Tejon Street.

Binding arbitration through the county is final and cannot be reviewed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Senior exemption and deferral

A senior exemption exists when the state pays for it. It can erase up to 50% of the first $200,000 of a primary residence's value, and lawmakers restored funding for tax year 2026, payable in 2027.

First-time applicants need to be 65 by January 1, and to have owned and occupied the home for a minimum of 10 consecutive years. Surviving spouses use a different route. The application deadline moves, so call (719) 520-6600 for the current date. Colorado also offers a senior deferral. Think of it as a state treasurer loan, recorded as a lien and accruing interest from May 1. Selling the home or transferring title makes it payable.

Selling with taxes owed

Owing tax doesn't stop a sale. The typical sequence:

  1. Title staff request the payoff figure from the County Treasurer.
  2. Back tax and interest show as a payoff line and are subtracted from what you receive.
  3. A recorded deferral gets paid off too, because selling ends it.
  4. Once an account has been auctioned, the lien buyer's payoff is added to the tax.

Expect the title company to record the deed once funds clear. If you inherited the house or can't find old statements, the County Treasurer's portal lets you look up the parcel and see what is owed before you list.

Have your latest statement handy, with your school and any metro district named, when you first talk to the title officer. Anyone relocating or behind on a bill can also ask about an as-is cash sale, which skips repairs and showings. Owners near the western hills should check insurance and defensible space before listing, since the Waldo Canyon Fire of June 2012 destroyed 347 homes and buyers remember it.

Frequently asked questions

Who bills property tax in Colorado Springs?

The county treasurer, not the city. Colorado Springs sets a 3.009 mill levy for tax year 2025, yet El Paso County sends the statement and collects for all districts.

What is the interest rate on late Colorado Springs property tax?

One percent per month, starting right away. Partial payments aren't accepted.

When does Colorado Springs sell delinquent tax liens?

Every October, online through RealAuction. Overdue taxes are advertised the month before.

Where do I file a Colorado Springs property tax appeal?

Begin with the County Assessor at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300. If needed, escalate to the Board of Equalization by July 15.

What happens to a Colorado Springs tax deferral when I sell?

It becomes due on a sale or title transfer. The deferral is recorded as a lien and accrues interest from May 1.

One government for tax, value and deeds

Broomfield sits between Denver and Boulder along US 36 and US 287, and it is a city and a county at once. Its own Assessor, Treasurer and Clerk and Recorder all work from One DesCombes Drive, inside the George Di Ciero City and County Building. A single government values the house, mails the bill and files the deed.

Phone the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or the Assessor at 303-464-5819, or email assessor@broomfield.org.

The city dates from 1961, and the county was created by consolidation on November 15, 2001, using land from four counties. That date matters for old records: the online recording portal starts with documents recorded in November 2001, and anything earlier may be held in Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld.

Broomfield housing at a glance

The 2020 count was 74,112 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 79,174, within 32.97 square miles. Owner-occupants live in 62.7% of homes, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $664,500, and median gross rent is $2,126. Because six school districts reach into the city, your address decides which mill levy lands on your bill, and neighbors a mile apart can pay different amounts.

Due dates

Plan on three dates: February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second, and April 30 if you pay everything at once. Pay on or before them and there is no interest.

Notices are sent to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, around the third week of January by email or mail. A lender that pays from escrow should be asked to confirm. When the tax is under $25, only the full-tax option is available.

After a due date, call 303-438-6390 for updated figures.

Ways to pay

Payment can be made in cash, by check, by eCheck or by credit card. The card vendor adds 2.50% and an eCheck costs $2.50. Each online transaction is capped at $1,000,000.

Seniors can apply for tax deferral at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com. Separately, a Certificate of Taxes Due (C.R.S. 39-10-115) states that every tax is paid apart from items it lists as still owed. Ask your title company whether it will order one for your sale.

How values are set

Values are reset in odd-numbered years and carried forward through even ones unless the property changes. January 1 is the assessment date.

For the 2025 and 2026 reappraisals, the Assessor looks at residential sales between July 1, 2022 and June 30, 2024, counting only qualified arms-length sales. Homes are valued by the market approach under USPAP guidelines.

In an even year a notice arrives only after a change such as a finished basement, an addition or a demolition. Your tax is value times assessment rate times mill levy, where the legislature fixes the assessment rate and the taxing authorities set the levy.

How to protest your valuation

Real property protests go to the Assessor from May 1 to June 8. For personal property, the cutoff is June 30.

  • Online: the appeal portal at appeals.spatialest.com/co-broomfield, which includes a neighborhood sales map and document uploads.
  • Mail: the Real Property Protest Form, postmarked by June 8, to PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149.
  • In person: the Community Assistance Center in the main lobby of the City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated 7/1/2022 to 6/30/2024, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of record errors. A Notice of Determination is sent by June 30 for real property.

Disagree with the result? The Board of Equalization takes real property appeals until July 15 and personal property appeals until July 20. Hearings are remote, before an independent hearing officer, and the burden is on you to show that your value is the more accurate one. Evidence files must be 20 MB or smaller. The board's contact is clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9. Hearings run in late July and finish by August 5.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording a deed

A flat $43 covers the first page of any recorded document under the schedule effective June 1, 2026, and added pages cost nothing. The city's recording page breaks that into a $40 fee and a $3 surcharge per document.

The documentary fee adds $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500, and Treasurer's, public trustee's and sheriff's deeds are exempt. Recording staff work weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. You can mail, drop off, deliver or e-record.

Documents need a one-inch top and bottom margin and half-inch side margins, a return address and a signed check payable to the City and County of Broomfield. The office cannot give legal advice on which document to file.

Preparing the paperwork before you sell

A little organizing up front helps. Pull the last tax statement, the notice of value and any protest decision, and write down who pays the tax, you or your lender through escrow. Then call the Treasurer and ask for the current balance and for the interest that would apply if closing slips into the next month.

Next, check the recording side. The Recording Division wants a one-inch top and bottom margin, a return address and a signed check, so any deed you sign yourself should meet those formatting rules before it goes in. Most sellers never do this alone, because the title company files the deed, but it is good to know what the office will check.

Last, think about timing. A sale that closes between the February and June dates will have one half already paid, so the settlement statement should show a credit or a charge for the part of the year each side owns. Ask your closing agent to explain how that split was calculated.

Selling with tax due

Any property tax you still owe is paid by the title company out of your proceeds. Get current numbers from the Treasurer before picking a date, since interest grows each month. If you close in late winter, check whether the February first half has been paid.

Gather your last tax statement, your notice of value and the name of your lender if taxes are escrowed. If you pay your own taxes, make sure the owner-of-record address is current. With a cash buyer, you can skip the loan approval step, and the title company only needs the payoff and the deed to finish. That keeps the closing date in your hands, which helps when you are relocating or settling an estate on a deadline.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When are Broomfield property taxes due?

February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second, April 30 for one full payment. A missed date brings 1% interest the next month.

Does Broomfield have a separate county government?

Yes. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, so one government assesses, bills and records.

What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield valuation?

June 8 for real property. A Board of Equalization appeal comes next, due July 15.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?

Recording is a flat $43 per document under the June 1, 2026 schedule. The documentary fee, $0.01 per $100 above $500, is added to that.

Can I sell a Broomfield house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The closing agent settles the balance from your proceeds. For the exact amount, call the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or 303-438-6390.

Behind on Fort Collins property tax?

Get My Cash Offer →

Fort Collins housing at a glance

Fort Collins is the Larimer County seat, roughly 60 miles north of Denver, and it counted 169,810 residents in 2020, which made it the fourth largest city in Colorado. The wider county had a 2025 estimate of 377,292 people and 158,769 housing units, with 63.8% of occupied homes owned by the people living in them.

Homes near the Cache la Poudre River or Spring Creek can draw flood questions from buyers and lenders. The city's worst flood hit in late July 1997, and sellers in those areas should expect the topic to come up in a showing or an inspection.

Who sends the tax bill

Your city does not bill property tax. The Larimer County Treasurer mails the statement, collects payment and sends the money out to every taxing authority on your bill, including the school district, the city and any special districts. The Treasurer has no say in how much you owe.

  • Questions about value or how the tax was figured go to the Larimer County Assessor.
  • Payments, statements, delinquent balances and the lien sale go to the Treasurer and Public Trustee.
  • Once a mortgage is paid off and the lender stops paying your tax, the Treasurer's site explains how to get your own statement.

The Public Trustee side of the same office handles foreclosures and the release of deeds of trust under Title 38 of the Colorado Revised Statutes. That is the office that matters when an old loan still sits on the record.

Due dates and payment choices

Taxes are due on January 1 for the previous year, and you can pay in one of two ways. Partial payments are not accepted. A due date on a non-business day moves to the next business day.

Payment optionDue dateNotes
First halfEnd of FebruaryTwo equal installments
Second halfJune 15Pairs with the February payment
Full paymentApril 30One payment instead of two

If you sell mid-year, ask the closing company how the current year's share will be handled, because the bill in hand covers the year before.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The 2026 tax lien sale

The annual sale of tax liens on unpaid real estate is set for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026. It takes place at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch, 5280 Arena Circle, Loveland, in the Thomas McKee 4-H Community Building.

A Fort Collins owner with delinquent real estate tax should phone the Treasurer before that date. Investors who want to bid find their own information on the same site, so the sale draws from two sides: owners trying to clear a balance and buyers hunting for liens.

Online tools and other ways to pay

The Treasurer takes payment online, issues receipts, and offers eNotices and email reminders. For automated monthly payments, the office signed up with EquaPay by Autoagent, formerly EscrowTaxes. Any Larimer County property without mortgage escrow can use it.

  • Title companies sign in separately to order Certificates of Taxes Due.
  • Mortgage companies have a mass payment option.
  • Owners can change a mailing address, search property and tax records, and print a receipt.
  • Manufactured homes, business personal property and special assessments each have their own pages.

Payment and search pages are sometimes offline for maintenance, so do not leave a deadline payment to the last minute.

Schools and your tax area

Public schools in Fort Collins run through the Poudre School District, which also levies tax on your bill. The school boundary a house sits in is therefore part of its tax area, and it is worth confirming which districts apply before you quote any bill to a buyer. A buyer comparing two houses will often ask which district each one falls in, and the Larimer County Assessor can sort out which taxing authorities apply to a parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to do about taxes when you sell

An unpaid balance does not stop a sale, but it has to be dealt with before the deed changes hands. Here is the order that works for most sellers.

  1. Tell your title company early so it can order the Certificate of Taxes Due through the Treasurer's title login.
  2. Read the certificate for any prior year balance or lien.
  3. If the account is delinquent and the lien sale is close, call the Treasurer before the sale date.
  4. Pay the balance from your proceeds at closing.
  5. If a loan is being paid off, confirm the Public Trustee has what it needs to release the deed of trust.

A cash buyer goes through the same title steps. What you skip is the lender's appraisal and repair demands, which helps when a house is dated or needs work. Cash does not erase a tax lien or a deed of trust, though. Both still get paid or released through title, so check the balances first and you will know your real net before you agree to a price.

What to gather before you list

A little paperwork up front keeps a Fort Collins sale from stalling at the title stage. Pull these together before you accept an offer.

  • Your latest tax statement, or a printed receipt from the Treasurer's site showing what has been paid.
  • The parcel's tax and property record from the county search, so you can match the legal owner name and address to what title will see.
  • Payoff information from your mortgage servicer, if a loan is still open.
  • Any notice about a special assessment, since those are billed on their own pages and can be missed.
  • For a manufactured home, the separate records the Treasurer keeps for that type of property.

Owners who have been paying through mortgage escrow sometimes never see the county bill. If that is you, ask your servicer for the last statement it paid so the numbers line up with the certificate.

From offer to closing

The tax piece moves in a predictable order whether the buyer uses a loan or pays cash. The title company opens a file, orders the Certificate of Taxes Due, and reviews it with the rest of the title search. Anything owed shows up there. If a lien is attached to the account, the title company tells you the payoff and plans to settle it from your proceeds.

Because the bill you hold covers the previous year, the current year's share is the open question at a mid-year closing. Your closing company will say how it is divided between you and the buyer, and you should read that line on the settlement statement before you sign.

After closing, the new owner updates the mailing address with the county so statements reach the right person. Sellers should do the same for any final notices, using the address change option on the Treasurer's site.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay property tax to in Fort Collins?

You pay the Larimer County Treasurer, not the city. The Treasurer collects for the school district, the city, the county and special districts.

When is the next Larimer County tax lien sale?

It is set for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch in Loveland.

Can I pay Fort Collins property tax in installments?

Yes. You can pay two equal installments or one full payment, but partial payments are not accepted. Owners without escrow can also enroll in EquaPay for monthly payments.

Which office do I call if I disagree with my value?

Call the Larimer County Assessor. The Treasurer does not determine the amount of tax and sends value questions there.

Can I sell a Fort Collins house that has tax due?

Yes. Your title company orders a Certificate of Taxes Due, and any balance is paid at closing. If the account is delinquent, call the Treasurer before the November lien sale.
